items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: the first record that really drew me in was this trumpet player, Phil, gave me a record by the Candoli brothers.

ctx.x: I love watching, playing with older fellas, you not only learn the music you watch how they operate with the audience, and taking requests and the whole thing about playing a gig.

Yeah. I understood the professional context of it, that this was a job. It wasn’t just get out there and show how fast you can play or whatever. Because always for me it was about the act of making music. And I really didn’t have a lot of repertoire. I didn’t study in the way of kind of building a repertoire for myself. It was like go and play and figure out what was going on in the moment. I was quite improvisational at that point. But I was also studying music. I started playing classical guitar in high school.…
